360394f33e3e2f99029aa4cd8fae22bad3ef8ae2.summary: A first-draft technical article from a personal Mac blog, published 2020-11-16, that explains how macOS 10.15 Catalina and 11.0 Big Sur check executable code before loading it. The checks described are a hash lookup against a local security database, reporting of unseen hashes to Apple, a known-malware check by XProtect, and online OCSP certificate revocation checks. It also covers Apple's stated privacy position and planned opt-out changes, and options for muting these checks. It is not a report on a specific malware family, campaign or incident.

hedges: The author calls this a first draft and asks readers to help correct its errors.
The author does not think the sending of new hashes has anything to do with notarization.
The hash lookup appears to check code against a database of known malware.
Earlier certificate checking appears to have been local; the author says Apple appears to have changed this.
The author says the OCSP exchange and hash transmission could conceivably be used against some journalists.
The author presumes Apple's planned opt-out would cover both hash lookup and certificate revocation checks.

36306e003905c18244827376abe525ad46e1a655.summary: Microsoft threat analysts linked the financially motivated group FIN7, also tracked as Sangria Tempest, to an April 2023 campaign deploying Clop ransomware. The attacks used the POWERTRASH dropper and the Lizar tool, with OpenSSH and Impacket for lateral movement. Microsoft also linked FIN7 to PaperCut printing server attacks using Clop, Bl00dy and LockBit, and tied FIN11 (Lace Tempest) to FIN7 tooling. The article recounts FIN7's history since 2013, including attacks on banks and point-of-sale terminals, USB lures, and prison sentences for several members in 2021 and 2022.

3647d0b1f55f78d0fd793ebc76728e2aecddd9f0.summary: The page is titled as a report on PolinRider, described as a DPRK threat actor implanting malware in hundreds of GitHub repositories. The body contains no analysis. It is a long numbered list of repository names, owners and project descriptions, with no malware behaviour, attribution, activity dates or indicators stated. It is classified as not a threat report because it is an index.
